newsitem.title: CANADA: Focus on Bombardier ahead of plane order.
newsitem.headline: Focus on Bombardier ahead of plane order.

text.p: Analysts were closely watching aerospace manufacturer Bombardier Inc on Monday ahead of an announcement expected by AMR Corp's American Eagle airlines on a US$1 billion-plus plane order.
American Eagle was expected to announce within the next few days an order for about 67 planes, either from Bombardier's Canadair or from Brazil's state-owned Embraer SA, or from both.
Analysts in Canada said there was speculation that an announcement on the order, worth more than US$1 billion, would be made at the Paris air show on Tuesday.

Canadair spokeswoman Catherine Chase told Reuters today that Bombardier was "in discussions," but she declined to specify with whom, adding that the company had not scheduled a news conference for Tuesday at the Paris air show.
"We are in negotiation and when a customer reaches a decision and is ready to make that public, if we are invovled, (we) will be very happy to do so," Chase said.
In the competition for the American Eagle order, Bombardier's 50-seat Canadair Regional Jet is competing with Embraer's EMB-145 50-seat twin-engine jet.
Analyst Margaret Cornish-Kehoe, of ScotiaMcLeod, said she was skeptical of speculation that American Eagle might split the order between Canadair and Embraer.
"All of this talk over the last couple of weeks about whether they have it or don't have it is just American Airlines trying to bring pricing pressure on Bombardier," she said.

Cornish-Kehoe said American Eagle might be concerned whether Bombardier could deliver the jets fast enough, since Bombardier had commitments to deliver other Regional Jets in 1998 for other customers.
"Whatever they choose, they want them in a hurry. Maybe that is the rationale for the split, but I think Bombardier can deliver then quite fast," she said.
Bombardier class B shares were unchanged at 30.20 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday, after rising 0.30 earlier.
